comment: The vectors pinning Prima.LocusBackends, the backends wire between CYFR's controller and the backends service Locus serves; apps/prima/test/prima/locus_backends_test.exs consumes every section, and every end of the wire (the Locus service, CYFR's client and the image probe) reproduces them. Every consumer derives the control, seal and owner keys from the service key over the label, reproduces each control message's and the invoke's canonical string, MAC and header, reads each control body and its answer to its members and writes them back to the same bytes, opens the sealed environment for its owner and lifetime only, parses every accepted header, refuses every malformed one as its kind and every one at another version token (v2) as unknown_version, refuses every invalid message with the error named and answers it with the refusal named, refuses every header under auth_rejected at its instant with its reason, and masks the input to the output. Integers are decimal in canonical strings and headers, and a header names its body's hex SHA-256 as body=, which an accepted header parses to as its body_hash. reserved_env_prefixes is Prima.KeeperProtocol's list, which the wire reserves. The fences are the service's, against state the wire does not hold: every fence_rejected vector runs against a fresh service at the boot the control vectors name, under the service key, each message presented at its now, with its headers beside its signature, and answered at its status until the refused one, which is the held message if one is held (its head sent and its body sent only once every later message is answered), else the last; it is refused with the code named, its body unread where read_body is false. advance_ms moves the service's lease clock; given names the pool its launcher answers ("unavailable" for none, 64 free uids otherwise), the live nonces the owner's cache already holds, and the stderr each backend process writes as it starts.
label: cyfr-locus/v1/backends
